Q: How to set retention period in AWS S3 A:

Your Error:

MethodNotAllowed The specified method is not allowed against this resource.

I would assume this means your PUT method is not valid. Try GET.
"Method" could mean something else. I am not familiar with S3. I'm just guessing.

Another thing I noticed about using curl is all the requests I fond on various site is they use a Signature hash.
Example: How to upload files on AWS S3 by using curl

I could not find any documentation on using curl. I did find this

Define the Object Lock feature configuration parameters by specifying the retention mode and retention period for the new S3 bucket. The following example enables Governance retention mode for 90 days. Governance mode ensures that users cannot overwrite or delete an S3 object version or alter its lock settings unless they have special permissions (e.g. root account access). Governance mode enables you to protect objects against deletion by most users while still allowing you to grant some users permission to alter the retention settings or delete the object if required.
Save these configuration parameters to a JSON file named object-lock-config.json:

{
  "ObjectLockEnabled": "Enabled",
  "Rule": {
    "DefaultRetention": {
      "Mode": "GOVERNANCE",
      "Days": 90
    }
  }
}

You have an XML error.
I am not saying it will work after fixing this error.
But it definitely will not work with an XML error.

Move the </Request> to the end:

<Request><Login>${ACCESS_KEY_ID}</Login><Password>${SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}</Password>
<ObjectLockConfiguration>
<ObjectLockEnabled>Enabled</ObjectLockEnabled>
<Rule><DefaultRetention>
<Mode>COMPLIANCE</Mode>
<Years>${RETYEARS}</Years>
</DefaultRetention></Rule>
</ObjectLockConfiguration></Request>

I used this online tool to find the error: XML Validator

Q: GraphQL Error : Field is not defined in the input type A:

According to the error message, it seems to be you forgot to reference the Article model with another related model(s). In Prisma, you can use something similar to this: references: [id] and in GraphCMS find the Reference button on the Add Field menu on the top right.

Q: ServerSelectionTimeoutError errno 11001 getaddrinfo failed python A:

The URI should be like "mongodb://username:password@host", where the host is the hostname or IP.

This happened to me when I was connecting with the name, but the host name changed, so I changed the URI to connect via the machine's IP.

Q: How to write automation tests for elements/processes that are frequently used elsewhere? A:

option 2, but the standalone test isnt one line. keep the shared helper action-only and give the calendar its own spec that exercises its actual behaviour.

```js

// helpers/calendar.js - no assertions, just does the thing

export const pickDate = (d) => {

cy.get('.rbc-calendar').should('be.visible')

cy.contains('.rbc-date-cell', d).click()

}

```

the calendar spec then covers month nav, disabled/past dates, range selection, whatever it actually does. calling `pickDate` once proves nothing.

if the helper asserts, one failure turns every booking test red and it looks like the booking flow broke rather than the calendar. waits and existence checks are ok, you need those for the click to land at all.behaviour checks are the ones that dont belong there.
